name: Zangersheide
notes: The Belgian jumping studbook at Lanaken, out of Leon Melchior's Zangersheide Stud of the 1970s and independent as Studbook Zangersheide from 1992. A registered horse carries Z after its name. It is a performance registry rather than a closed breed: Holsteiner, Hanoverian, Selle Francais, Dutch and Belgian Warmblood and Thoroughbred lines all qualify on jumping ability.
Jump 10, which is the one thing the whole studbook exists to select for. Speed 8 behind it, because a jumper needs an adjustable gallop rather than a flat-racing one.
A tall band, running to 17.2 hands at the top. The studbook enforces no height standard at all, which is why it is wide rather than tight.

Colour is not selected on at all, and the pool reflects that rather than forcing solid bay: grey and cream are ordinary, and tobiano, sabino, splash, W20, a trace of frame, roan, rabicano, dun and silver are all reachable. A pinto Z is a real horse, just an unusual one.
Champagne, pearl, mushroom, the leopard complex and brindle stay wild. An open registry is not a reason to give every locus a frequency.

WFFS is the warmblood disorder this breed would carry, and the locus exists in the mod - it is PLOD1. No rate is written here because the draft's own figure was a self-labelled warmblood proxy rather than a Zangersheide measurement, and it was declined. The breed ships clear of it for want of evidence, not because the gene is missing.
Every other disorder clear. An open pedigree is not a licence to import the Quarter Horse or Friesian panel.
Carries neither tolerance locus - a modern international sport horse that lives in a stable, like the other warmbloods here.
Managed only: cowboy, spawn egg and stable, no wild herds.
